prompt.context: Insuraco is a large US insurer that is looking to grow. They currently sell a wide range of insurance products to US consumers and are considering developing a new product: $5/month smartphone insurance for under-30s. Insuraco's management is excited about the opportunity of selling to this large, under-insured group.
prompt.question: Before they develop the idea further, they'd like to know: (1) whether this is indeed a good idea, and (2) if so, how they should roll out this new product.

clarifying_info.a: To maximize profit, particularly in the first year the product is released.

clarifying_info.q: How does Insuraco currently sell its products?

clarifying_info.a: Only the US. Insuraco is licensed to sell in all US states.

clarifying_info.q: Should investment income be included in financial calculations?
clarifying_info.a: No, investment income can be ignored.

exhibits.title: Insuraco's Potential Distribution Channels — 1st Year Projections
exhibits.shows: A table comparing two distribution channels (Website vs. Agents) across four metrics: Development Costs, Year 1 expected website visits/agent enquiries, Conversion Rate, and Combined Ratio. A note states that average contract length at end of first year is 6 months, and Insuraco will only invest in one channel for this product.

data.note: Average contract length at end of first year is 6 months; Insuraco will only invest in one channel

exhibits.title: Combined Ratio Definition
exhibits.shows: The formula for Combined Ratio: Total Costs (i.e. Claims & Operating Expenses) divided by Total Revenue (i.e. Premium). A footnote states this does not include Development Costs.

data.formula: Combined Ratio = Total Costs (Claims & Operating Expenses) / Total Revenue (Premium)

framework: Is the market attractive? — Size & Growth: estimate annual revenue of under-30s smartphone insurance market in the US
Is the market attractive? — Competition: assess existing competitors and substitutes
Is the market attractive? — Customers: understand buying preferences and willingness to pay
Can Insuraco enter effectively? — Product: define coverage and pricing ($5/month, standard causes of loss/damage)
Can Insuraco enter effectively? — Capabilities: evaluate Insuraco's pricing expertise, brand, and distribution options (website vs. agents)

questions.prompt: Estimate the annual revenue of the US under-30s smartphone insurance market.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a top-down chain: US Population × % under 30 × % owning a smartphone (split by age band) × % interested in insurance × % willing to pay × annual premium. Structure and reasoning matter more than the exact number. A figure around $100m/year is acceptable.

math.setup: US Population × % under 30 × % owning smartphone × % interested in insurance × % willing to pay × annual premium per customer
steps: % under 30: assume equal age distribution, so 30 × 4m = 120m → 120m/320m ≈ 37.5%, round to ~35% → 112m under-30s
% owning a smartphone: assume 0% for under-15s (half of group), 80% for 15-to-30-year-olds → blended ~40% → 45m
% interested in smartphone insurance: insurance is underused by this group → ~20% → 9m
% willing to pay: again expected low → ~20% → 1.8m

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the Year 1 profitability of the Website channel and the Agents channel. Which channel should Insuraco choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2 (Combined Ratio definition). Key steps: compute paying customers = visits × conversion rate; compute average annual profit per customer = monthly premium × avg contract months × (1 − combined ratio); compute operating profit = customers × profit per customer; subtract development costs. Candidate should initially identify Agents as better ($25k vs −$10k). Interviewer then reveals that a 10% increase in website development costs raises conversion to 30% — recalculate and note both channels yield $25k first-year profit. Candidate should then recommend Website because development costs are a one-time expense, making it more profitable in subsequent years.

math.setup: Paying customers = visits/enquiries × conversion rate; Avg profit/customer = $5/month × 6 months × (1 − combined ratio); Operating profit = customers × avg profit; Net profit = operating profit − development costs
steps: Both channels now yield $25k in Year 1
Since development costs are one-time, Website is more profitable from Year 2 onward
Bonus: avg contract length of 3 years further amplifies website advantage long-term
math.answer: Both channels yield $25k first-year profit after the website cost revision; Website is preferred long-term because its development cost is a one-time expense

questions.prompt: What non-financial considerations should Insuraco address in rolling out this product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure qualitative factors into clear buckets. Strong answers cover: marketing/branding relevance to under-30s; Insuraco's internal capabilities for this demographic; risk to existing agent relationships; competitive response and differentiation; growth and cross-sell opportunities.

brainstorming.prompt: What other (non-financial) considerations need to be made regarding the roll-out of this new product?

categories.name: Marketing & Branding
ideas: How can Insuraco make insurance relevant, cool, and desirable to under-30s?
Does Insuraco have internal marketing capability for this demographic, or must it hire new expertise?
Should Insuraco create a new brand (sub-brand) rather than sell under its existing conservative brand?

categories.name: Agent Relationship Management
ideas: Insuraco currently sells all products through agents — adopting a direct website channel could damage those relationships
Needs a strategy to manage agent channel conflict

categories.name: Competitive Response
ideas: Product is easily replicable (standard coverage, no novel features)
How can Insuraco differentiate and defend first-mover advantage?
Insurers already offer smartphone coverage bundled in home/contents insurance — they could un-bundle it quickly

categories.name: Growth Opportunities
ideas: Launching smartphone insurance opens the door to selling other products to under-30s (travel, renters, auto)
Building brand loyalty early could secure customers for higher-value products later (homeowners, life, medical insurance)
Cross-sell and up-sell potential once customer relationship is established

recommendation: Insuraco should launch the $5/month smartphone insurance product for under-30s via a new website channel
The market is large (~$100m annual revenue), currently competitor-free, and profitable (combined ratio below 100%)

With revised website investment (+10% dev cost), both channels yield equal first-year profit of $25k, but the website is superior long-term because development costs are a one-time expense and it signs up more customers
risks: Uncertainty around future number of website visits and agent enquiries — long-term profitability depends on these unknown volumes
Combined ratios and conversion rates are assumed stable; adverse claims experience or lower conversion could erode margins
Launching a direct website channel risks damaging existing agent relationships on which all other Insuraco products depend
next_steps: Conduct market research to understand future trends in website traffic and agent enquiry volumes
Develop a marketing and branding strategy tailored to under-30s
Proactively manage agent relationships and address potential channel conflict
Assess competitive response and build differentiation (brand, UX, bundling)
Explore adjacent products to cross-sell to the under-30 customer base
